The employment outlook will be Good for power engineers and power systems operators (NOC 92100) in Newfoundland and Labrador for the 2025-2027 period.

The following factors contributed to this outlook:

  • Employment growth will lead to a few new positions.

Here are some key facts about power engineers and power systems operators in Newfoundland and Labrador:

  • Approximately 650 people work in this occupation.
  • Power engineers and power systems operators mainly work in the following sectors:
    • Utilities (NAICS 22): 20%
    • Mining and quarrying (NAICS 212): 12%
    • Hospitals (NAICS 622): 11%

    • apprenticeship or trades certificate or diploma: 35% compared to 17% for all occupations

The employment outlook will be Good for power engineers and power systems operators (NOC 92100) in New Brunswick for the 2025-2027 period.

  • Employment growth will lead to a moderate number of new positions.
  • A moderate number of positions will become available due to retirements.
  • There are a moderate number of unemployed workers with recent experience in this occupation.
  • Power engineers and power systems operators are employed in sectors involving energy generation, such as utilities and manufacturing.
  • A strong demand for electricity, including clean energy, is driving the demand for power engineers and power systems operators.
  • A valid Power Engineer License from the Government of New Brunswick is often required by employers. These licenses require a combination of on the job and technical training.
